title: He let bees sting his nose on purpose
label: STUNG. *ON PURPOSE.*

lines.text: He let bees sting his face, on purpose.
Bee scientist Michael Smith wanted to know where stings hurt most. So he tested twenty five spots, on himself.
Five stings every morning, each stinger left in for a full minute.
Skull, toe and upper arm? Barely two out of ten.
Ow! My lip! That's almost a nine!
lines.speaker: smith

lines.text: And the worst spot of all? Right up the nose.
Thirty eight days later, he had mapped where stings hurt most. And he was fine.

experiment.fish: #20 (a Cornell scientist stung himself in 25 places to rank the pain)
experiment.hypothesis: First Short narrated by Chatterbox michael (george's pick, 28 Nov) instead of Kokoro; plain he_statement hook; a character line in its own voice with a moving mouth; calmer face brightness.

facts.claim: Cornell graduate student Michael L. Smith stung himself at 25 body locations, five stings a day between 20 August and 26 September 2012 (38 days), each bee held to the spot with forceps, and rated the pain from 1 to 10 against his forearm.
Most painful: nostril 9.0, upper lip 8.7. Least painful: skull, middle toe tip and upper arm, each 2.3.
